title: The Anxious Generation
author: Jonathan Haidt
blurb: Around 2012, rates of anxiety, depression, and self-harm among teenagers began rising sharply across many wealthy countries. Social psychologist Jonathan Haidt argues the main cause was a Great Rewiring of childhood. In just a few years, kids moved from a play-based childhood, full of unsupervised time with friends, to a phone-based childhood spent on smartphones and social media. At the same time, fearful parenting cut back on the free play and independence children need to grow resilient. Haidt describes how this shift deprives kids of sleep, face-to-face connection, and focus, and how it fuels addiction. He explains why girls and boys tend to be harmed in different ways. Finally, he proposes four simple norms that families and schools can adopt together, because no single parent can solve this collective problem alone.

lessons.b: In the early 2010s, teen mental health declined sharply just as childhood moved from playgrounds to smartphones and social media.
issues: scene 8: The frame is mostly text. The before/after illustration is small and crammed into the lower-left corner, and the whole right half of the stage is empty. The picture barely carries the reflection prompt. (fix: Enlarge the before/after panels so they become the main visual, about 2x larger, and place them on the right half beside the questions. Alternatively, keep the text on the left and put the two panels stacked or side by side on the right, so the layout is balanced and the illustration reads clearly.)

lessons.t: Children Need Free Play to Grow
lessons.b: Unsupervised, slightly risky play is how kids build resilience, because children are antifragile and grow stronger through small challenges.
Adults shielded kids from minor real-world risks while leaving them almost unprotected in a virtual world never designed for children.
issues: scene 2: In the 'Play in the park' card, the amber circle sits on top of the slide and the X strokes. The icon reads as a muddled stack of shapes rather than a clear park scene. (fix: Move the amber ball or sun clear of the slide, for example to the upper-left of the card behind the X, or shrink it so it doesn't overlap the playground structure.)

scene 8: The 'LOOSEN' and 'TIGHTEN' labels and their icons are tiny, at or under about 18px at 1600 width. They are crowded into the lower right, leaving the visual nearly negligible next to the large text. (fix: Scale the tree and locked-phone icons up about 2x and raise the label size to at least 22px. Position them as a balanced visual element beside or below the question rather than as a small footnote.)

lessons.b: Phone-based childhood damages kids through social deprivation, sleep deprivation, fragmented attention, and addiction.

lessons.t: Why Social Media Hits Girls Hardest
lessons.b: Image-based social media exploits girls' sensitivity to social comparison and relational aggression, driving higher rates of anxiety and depression.
